what: One record per entity that appears on a shareholder register the terminal holds, with every security it appears on. Built from the registers only; no name is invented and no link is inferred.
caveats: A NOMINEE OR CUSTODY ACCOUNT IS NOT AN OWNER. Names such as 'Kenya Commercial Bank Nominees Limited A/C 915' hold shares for clients whose identity the register does not give. Their links are kept, because where a stake sits in custody is a real fact, but counts_as_ownership is false and they must not be drawn as a relationship between the companies they appear on.
A FUND MANAGER usually holds on behalf of many underlying funds, so its links are also marked counts_as_ownership false.

Names are merged only when they normalise identically after case, punctuation and corporate suffixes. Near misses are listed under review and are NOT merged, because automatically fusing owner names asserts that two parties are one.
Every holding carries the as-of date of the register it came from. Registers are annual at best and some are years old, so two holdings on one entity may describe different moments.
A register lists the top holders only, so absence from this file is not evidence that an entity holds nothing.
